user.title: Connect to your bridge
user.description:
Enter the network address of the RS485 bridge that listens to your bus (for example an Elfin EW11 in transparent mode). Modbus Tap only listens; it never sends anything on the bus.

Still wiring things up? See the [tapping guide]({guide}).

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the bridge.
data_description.port: TCP port of the bridge's transparent socket (8899 on Elfin devices).

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't open a connection. Check the address and that the bridge accepts another client.

abort.already_configured: This bridge is already set up.

sensors.title: Sensors

unit_map.title: Register map for unit {unit}
unit_map.description:
{heard}

**1. Start from a community map** if one fits your device. Available:
{maps}

**2. Add or correct entries** in the box below, in the core Modbus sensor format. Your entries replace community entries with the same table and address. Leave it empty to use the community map as it is.

Example:
```yaml
- name: Grid voltage
  address: 37
  input_type: input
  scale: 0.1
  precision: 1
  unit_of_measurement: V
  device_class: voltage
```
No idea what the registers mean? Make a recording first (Configure → Recordings). [Register map guide]({docs})

data_description.community_map: Ready-made sensors for a device model. Suggested when this unit matches one.
data_description.overrides: Optional. Saving reloads Modbus Tap so the sensors update.

recordings.title: Recordings
recordings.description:
{state} {sources}

A recording logs all bus traffic next to values you already have. It doesn't change your sensors by itself: use **Suggest a register map** to turn it into sensors, or download it and work it out yourself. [How it works]({docs})

menu_options.recording_analyse: Suggest a register map from a recording

recording_start.title: Start a recording
recording_start.description:
Logged next to the bus traffic: {references}.

Let it run while things change (sun, clouds, appliances on and off). The **Stop recording** button on the bridge device ends it early.

recording_control.title: Stop the recording
recording_control.description: **{name}** is running. Submit to stop it; a notification will link to the file.

recording_sources.title: Reference sources and storage
recording_sources.description: Values logged next to the bus traffic in every recording: your answer key for matching registers. They're only used while recording, so you can clear them once your map works, and an unavailable or removed source never breaks anything. Changes apply from the next recording. [Which to use?]({docs})

data_description.reference_devices: Every sensor of these devices is logged. Pick the device of your inverter's cloud integration to get all its values at once.
data_description.reference_patterns: For sensors without a device, such as those posted by an add-on. Use * as a wildcard, for example `sensor.solarsynkv3_*`.

recording_files.title: Download or delete recordings

recording_analyse.title: Suggest a register map
recording_analyse.description:
Modbus Tap looks for registers that follow your reference entities in the recording, and works out their scale. You review the result before anything changes.

{ai} [How matching works]({docs})

data_description.recording: Newest first. A few hours with things changing works best.
data_description.unit: The unit to suggest sensors for.
data_description.ai_task: An AI Task entity. It gets a summary of the recording (no raw file) and may add registers Modbus Tap can't match on its own, such as counters and states.

suggestion.title: Suggested sensors for unit {unit}
suggestion.description:
{notes}

Edit or remove entries below, then submit to add them to the unit's own entries. Entries at the same address are replaced; the rest of your map stays. Saving reloads Modbus Tap.

data_description.overrides: Entries with `verified` closely followed a reference entity. The others are guesses: compare them with your reference values for a day.

writes.title: Writes

data_description.clear: Starts the history afresh. Leave off to just close this screen.

error.invalid_unit: Enter a unit address from 1 to 247.

abort.not_loaded: Modbus Tap isn't running right now. Try again once it has started.
abort.no_recordings: No recordings yet. Use Start or stop a recording, or the Start recording button on the bridge device.
abort.nothing_to_export: No register maps yet. Set one up under Sensors first.
abort.recording_started: Recording started. Stop it with the Stop recording button on the bridge device, or here.
abort.recording_stopped: Recording stopped. A notification links to the file. Next: turn it into a register map (see the Recordings guide), then paste it under Sensors.
abort.no_writes: The poller hasn't written anything since Modbus Tap started keeping track. Many pollers only read; others write every few minutes or only when a setting changes.

silent.title: Modbus Tap hears nothing on {title}
silent.description: The bridge is connected, but no bytes have arrived for over ten minutes. Check the wiring between the bus and the bridge, and that the poller is running.

reversed.title: Modbus Tap can't decode the bus on {title}
reversed.description: Data arrives but no valid Modbus frames, and it's mostly zero bytes. That usually means the A and B wires are swapped. Swapping them is harmless; try that first, then check the baud rate.

undecodable.title: Modbus Tap can't decode the bus on {title}
undecodable.description: Data arrives but no valid Modbus frames. Check the bridge's baud rate and parity first (save and reboot the bridge after each change), then try swapping A and B.

confirm.title: Use the {map} community map?
confirm.description: Unit {unit} matches the community map for the {map}. Use it as the base for this unit's register map? Your own entries stay on top.
